expected.summary: The TLS certificate on the Elasticsearch cluster that search queries (catalog-index.search.svc, CN=*.search.svc, issued by internal-ca) expired nine minutes before the anchor and was never renewed; search pods had logged tls.expiry warnings every ten minutes for the hour before. search holds pooled keep-alive connections to Elasticsearch, so failures began as a trickle and climbed over about five minutes to roughly 95 percent of search requests as the pool recycled and every new TLS handshake was rejected with CERT_HAS_EXPIRED. The failing search.query spans end within a few milliseconds and have no es.search child, so search latency fell while its error rate rose; catalog and pricing are simply no longer called from /search and stay healthy on every other route. Nothing was deployed and no version changed. web-bff and mobile-bff pass the 503s on as 502s and the failures reach edge-gateway, two hops downstream, where the alert fires. Only GET /search is affected. The periodic catalog reindex that writes to catalog-index is routine and unrelated.
contributingFactors: Elasticsearch TLS certificate behind search expired without renewal
keep-alive connection pool recycling onto new handshakes that all fail

criteria.description: Does the brief place the origin at search's Elasticsearch cluster (catalog-index) presenting an expired TLS certificate, so search's handshakes fail, with edge-gateway two hops downstream as a victim? 5 = expired certificate, search as the failing caller, the propagation path. Blaming catalog, pricing, the reindex or a deploy scores at most 1.

Is it grounded in the CERT_HAS_EXPIRED errors on search spans and logs, and ideally the tls.expiry warnings before onset or the gradual climb as pooled connections recycled? Cap at 3 if it names a certificate problem without citing the error text or the expiry warnings.
Does it avoid claiming a deploy (there was none), avoid treating search's falling latency as recovery, and avoid blaming search's callees or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
